blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Spatial instructions describe how to move objects, transform regions, or modify their surroundings. When several operations are applied in sequence, each acts on a configuration shaped by earlier changes. How accurately can large language models (LLMs) predict the resulting spatial state? We introduce Grid-Bench, an executable benchmark in which eight families of operations transform discrete worlds represented as two-, three-, and four-dimensional grids. Given an initial grid, explicit rules, and an event history expressed as text, a model predicts the complete final grid. Reference execution makes every predicted value checkable, supporting comparisons across spatial operations, history lengths, and workloads. Evaluating six LLMs shows that complete-state accuracy falls sharply as histories grow, with substantial divergence among models that perform similarly on single events. Models with similar exact-match accuracy can nevertheless differ substantially in the number of incorrect cells on shared instances. Even over long histories, some models recover many correct changes beyond what copying the initial state would yield. Grid-Bench makes both complete recovery and these differences in returned states directly measurable across a range of spatial conditions.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Spatial reasoning supports understanding scene descriptions and interpreting
instructions about objects and their surroundings ( Shi et al., 2022 ; Long et al., 2016 ) . Such instructions appear in tasks ranging
from object manipulation to geometric design, where language specifies actions
or construction operations that change a spatial configuration ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ; Khan et al., 2024 ) . When instructions describe a
sequence of operations, earlier changes can alter the spatial conditions on which
later operations depend. Moving an object, for example, can free one position
while blocking another, changing the outcome of a subsequent move. Predicting
the resulting configuration from text therefore involves relating the described
operations to the spatial states they successively produce. We investigate how
accurately large language models predict these outcomes across varied operations,
event histories, and spatial structures.

We evaluate six large language models under a shared protocol and find that
exact-match accuracy declines sharply with history length. Models with similar
single-event accuracy separate over longer histories, and even similar rates
of complete recovery can accompany quite different incorrect predictions.

yet their median wrong-cell counts are 14 and 67 on the 84 shared instances
where both return valid incorrect states.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Spatial benchmarks evaluate relations, transformations, and actions through
different prediction targets.
SPARTQA ( Mirzaee et al., 2021 ) and SPARTUN/ReSQ ( Mirzaee and Kordjamshidi, 2022 ) ask questions about relations expressed in scene
descriptions. StepGame ( Shi et al., 2022 ) tests relational composition,
while SpaRC/SpaRP ( Rizvi et al., 2024 ) formalizes spatial properties and
reasoning paths.
Other evaluations consider constrained path construction ( Kaesberg et al., 2025 ) , spatial reasoning across textual and visual inputs ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , and action selection in symbolic or simulated
environments ( Gao et al., 2026b ; Gao et al., 2026a ) .
JigShape ( Li et al., 2026c ) evaluates geometric reconstruction from puzzle
pieces, and OrigamiBench ( Agarwal et al., 2026 ) studies physically grounded
fold operations.
SnorkelSpatial ( Vishwakarma, 2025 ) studies transformations of
textual boards, querying properties after translations and rotations.
Grid-Bench evaluates the complete configuration produced by a prescribed
event history, allowing errors to be located throughout the resulting world.

blocks.en:
Predicting the result of an event history also connects spatial reasoning to
instruction execution and state tracking. bAbI ( Weston et al., 2015 ) includes
questions about locations and possessions after narrated events; SCONE ( Long et al., 2016 ) grounds instruction sequences in executable worlds;
and ProPara ( Dalvi et al., 2018 ) follows entity existence and location
through procedural text. Entity-tracking
evaluations more directly test whether models update affected entities while
retaining unaffected information across operations ( Kim and Schuster, 2023 ; Tang et al., 2026 ) . Beyond state tracking, GT Bench ( Xu et al., 2026e ) examines
algorithmic reasoning over graphs, while AlgoWorlds ( Xu et al., 2026d ) evaluates tool-guided decisions against verifiable optima.
Closest to our complete-state setting,
Alien Grid ( Chapra et al., 2026 ) studies sequential depth through
rotations, corner swaps, and shifts of a 3 × 3 3\times 3 grid. Chess-World-Model ( Walker and Lyons, 2026 ) trains sequence models to recover complete chess states
at successive move prefixes. Grid-Bench evaluates LLMs given explicit textual
rules across geometric, neighborhood, connectivity, and movement operations,
using complete predictions to compare recovery across spatial conditions.
Appendix A develops these connections and compares the
corresponding evaluation settings.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
Grid-Bench uses eight families of executable operations and exact reference
states to evaluate how accurately language models predict the complete final
state of a discrete spatial world.
Across six models, success on individual operations gives way to much lower
exact recovery over longer histories, with substantial differences across
models and spatial conditions. When complete recovery fails, the returned
states range from nearly correct grids to extensively incorrect configurations.
Some retain many correct updates beyond what copying the initial state would
recover, even at the longest histories. Reliable prediction of spatial change
remains challenging even with explicit rules. The executable rules can supply
training examples with exact targets, while cell-level diagnostics can show
whether models improve at predicting required changes, preserving unchanged
values, or both.

blocks.en:

spatial conditions studied here. Transfer to other world sizes, operation
distributions, or environments with uncertain observations remains an empirical

described world and a sequence of operations to an observable outcome. This

blocks.en: A.1 Spatial relations, perception, and action
blocks.zh: A.1 空间关系、感知和行动

blocks.en:
Textual spatial benchmarks have progressively broadened the relations and
compositions exposed in language. SPARTQA asks relation, object, and containment
questions over human-written and generated scene descriptions ( Mirzaee et al., 2021 ) ; SPARTUN and ReSQ broaden relation types, linguistic
expressions, and human-authored questions ( Mirzaee and Kordjamshidi, 2022 ) . StepGame
varies the length of relation chains and the presence of distractors ( Shi et al., 2022 ) , and later analysis separates relation parsing from
logical composition while correcting template artifacts ( Li et al., 2024 ) . SpaRC formalizes properties of objects, relations, and
contexts, while SpaRP supplies deductively verified reasoning paths ( Rizvi et al., 2024 ) .

逻辑组成在纠正模板文物的同时(Li等人,2024年). SpaRC 将对象、关系和
(Rizvi等人,2024年)。

blocks.en:
Visual benchmarks provide a complementary tradition of controlled spatial
evaluation. CLEVR uses rendered scenes and generated questions to diagnose
compositional visual reasoning ( Johnson et al., 2017 ) ; NLVR pairs natural
statements with synthetic images requiring visual and set-theoretic reasoning ( Suhr et al., 2017 ) . VSR evaluates natural text–image pairs across a broad
inventory of spatial relations and reference frames ( Liu et al., 2023b ) , while
SpatialEval compares spatial questions across textual and visual inputs ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . These benchmarks make relation recognition and
composition observable under different balances of perception and language.
JigShape extends geometric evaluation to reconstructing jigsaw arrangements
from interlocking pieces and visual content ( Li et al., 2026c ) . OrigamiBench
connects visual observations with a language of physically grounded fold
actions ( Agarwal et al., 2026 ) . FigEdit studies another form of structured
transformation: checking whether chart edits respect the intended data and
graphical relationships ( Li et al., 2026b ) .

blocks.en:
Maintaining a coherent visual world across time introduces further requirements.
CAT-NeRF separates appearance shared across a video from frame-specific body
variation ( Zhu et al., 2023 ) , while Memorize-and-Generate compresses prior
frames into memory to retain historical scene information during video
generation ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) . VISD uses feedback on answer correctness,
logical consistency, and spatiotemporal grounding to train video reasoning
models ( Lin et al., 2026 ) . Learning a symbolic description from observations
is a related problem: abductive state grounding uses environmental knowledge
to supervise the mapping from sensory inputs to symbolic states ( Su et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
长期维持一个连贯的视觉世界提出了进一步的要求。

逻辑一致性,以及用于培训视频推理的瞬间定位
模型 (Lin et al., 2026). 从观察中学习象征性描述
是一个相关的问题:利用环境知识进行绑架性国家搁浅
以监督从感官输入到象征状态的绘图(Su等人,2026年)。

blocks.en:
Changes in the external world also affect the knowledge needed to answer visual
questions. LiveVQA evaluates seeking and updating recent visual knowledge ( Fu et al., 2025 ) ; Worldwide LiveVQA extends this setting across languages,
with entity-recognition and multi-hop questions ( Huang et al., 2026 ) .
These evaluations concern keeping knowledge current as new observations become
available. Grid-Bench supplies the initial world and the events that determine
the requested final state.

问题。 LiveVQA评价了寻求和更新最新视觉知识的情况(Fu等人,2025年);Worldwide LiveVQA将这一设置扩展到各种语言,

这些评价涉及随着新的观测结果的出现而保持知识的及时性。

blocks.en:
Other work places spatial reasoning inside path construction or interactive
action selection. SPaRC pathfinding asks models to construct grid paths under
interacting spatial, arithmetic, and geometric constraints ( Kaesberg et al., 2025 ) . TextWorld generates executable text games with
controllable worlds and quests ( Côté et al., 2018 ) ; ALFWorld aligns such
textual interaction with embodied household environments ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ) , and ScienceWorld provides an interactive text
environment for scientific tasks ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . More recent
spatial-agent evaluations include iVISPAR’s sliding-tile tasks across text, 2D,
and 3D inputs ( Mayer et al., 2025 ) , CubeBench’s symbolic and visual cube
manipulation ( Gao et al., 2026b ) , and SpatialWorld’s egocentric multimodal
environments ( Gao et al., 2026a ) . Three-Step Nav combines landmark
planning, local visual guidance, and trajectory review for language-guided
navigation ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) . Ponder & Press separates instruction
interpretation from locating interface elements for computer control ( Wang et al., 2025d ) . These settings evaluate paths or
actions selected toward a goal. Grid-Bench instead supplies the operations and
evaluates the complete configuration they produce.

blocks.en: A.2 Instruction execution and entity state
blocks.zh: A.2 指令执行和实体国家

blocks.en:
Controlled language tasks have long connected narrated events to changing
worlds. bAbI generates questions about locations, possessions, and other facts
after sequences of events ( Weston et al., 2015 ) . SCONE pairs an initial world
with context-dependent instructions in three executable domains; predicted
logical forms are evaluated by the world they produce ( Long et al., 2016 ) . Both use simulation to make consequences checkable, while
placing different demands on the predicted answer.
blocks.zh:
控制的语言任务将描述的事件与变化长期连接
诸世界. bAbI产生关于地点、财产和其他事实的问题
在事件序列之后(Weston等人,2015年). SCONE 初始世界对齐
包含三个可执行域中上下文依赖的指令; 预测
逻辑形式由其产生的世界来评价(Long等人,2016年)。 两者都使用模拟使后果可以检查,而
对预测的答案提出不同要求。

blocks.en:
Procedural-text research studies changes that may be implicit in natural
descriptions. Neural Process Networks model actions as operators that transform
learned entity states ( Bosselut et al., 2018 ) . ProPara annotates entity
existence and location as a process unfolds ( Dalvi et al., 2018 ) , and OpenPI
extends procedural state changes to open-vocabulary entities, attributes, and
before/after values ( Tandon et al., 2020 ) . TRIP associates multi-sentence
physical stories with state annotations that support tiered evaluation of
plausibility and its underlying evidence ( Storks et al., 2021 ) . This line asks
models to infer consequences from ordinary language; Grid-Bench makes the
transition rules explicit and varies the spatial structures on which they act.

说明。 神经过程网络作为转换操作器的模型动作

在数值之前/之后(Tandon等人,2020年)。 TRIP 联系多人判决
有状态说明的物理故事支持对
可信度及其基本证据(Storks等人,2021年). 此行问
从普通语言推断后果的模型;
过渡规则明确,并改变它们采取行动的空间结构。

blocks.en:
Entity-tracking studies isolate update and retention more directly. Box-transfer
tasks query container contents after PUT, REMOVE, and MOVE operations and
distinguish changed from unchanged states ( Kim and Schuster, 2023 ) . Subsequent work
uses behavioral tests, probes, and interventions to study how models process
these changes ( Tang et al., 2026 ) . Related probing work recovers and
manipulates entity-state information in models trained on Alchemy instructions
and TextWorld transcripts ( Li et al., 2021 ) . These studies motivate
examining both final values that differ from the initial world and those that
match it when a model returns an entire state.

任务查询 PUT、REMOVE 和 Move 操作和
区分与不变状态(Kim and Schuster, 2023 ). 随后的工作

在受Alchemy指令培训的模型中操纵实体状态信息
和TextWorld的笔录(Li等人,2021年). 这些研究激励着:

匹配当一个模型返回整个状态时。

blocks.en:
The use of evolving histories also appears in social and personalized
interaction. SocialMaze evaluates reasoning across social settings with
changing interactions and uncertain information ( Xu et al., 2025d ) ;
PersonaConvBench evaluates personalized predictions and generation from
conversation histories ( Li et al., 2025b ) . Memory Retrieval for
Changing Preferences selects historical turns as evidence of a user’s current
preferences ( Qin et al., 2026 ) , while RaMem preserves temporal and
participant context when retrieving past experiences ( Yang et al., 2026b ) .
The scope of retained information matters as well: shared-state agents can
misapply information from one user’s interaction to another ( Yang et al., 2026a ) . For procedural memory, HyperSkill links reusable
skills and subtask steps through the trajectories in which they occurred ( Xu et al., 2026a ) . This literature examines which past information
remains useful and how it should be represented; spatial-state prediction
provides explicit operations whose consequences can be checked at the cell level.

blocks.en:
Board games provide deterministic state transitions over long sequences.

blocks.en: A.4 Sequential computation and structured reasoning

blocks.en:
Formal and synthetic tasks study how neural models realize computations over
sequences. Computation-graph analyses cover multiplication, logic-grid tasks,
and dynamic programming ( Dziri et al., 2023 ) . Automata experiments show that
the number of state transitions in a specification need not determine the
computation a Transformer learns ( Liu et al., 2023a ) ; evaluations across the
Chomsky hierarchy relate length generalization to task and architecture classes ( Delétang et al., 2023 ) . Permutation-composition studies combine behavioral
evaluation with probes and activation patching to examine learned algorithms ( Li et al., 2025a ) . Scratchpads instead expose intermediate computations as
generated text for tasks including program execution ( Nye et al., 2021 ) .
In multi-hop question answering, Wan et al. (2026) analyze single-pass
reasoning through an information-theoretic capacity model and use it to
motivate decomposition of interdependent evidence.

blocks.en:
Program analysis provides a setting in which intermediate claims have formal
semantics. Mitchell et al. (2025) prompt LLMs to reason as abstract
interpreters, evaluating the soundness of generated invariants and recurring
reasoning errors. For natural-language queries, Qin et al. (2025) instead
convert premises into logical representations and check them against retrieved
sources before generating a response.

blocks.en:
Graph-based methods expose another range of structural dependencies. NQE
combines neural representations of n-ary facts with logical query operations ( Luo et al., 2023 ) . GT Bench evaluates graph algorithms across graph structures
and input representations, and GTA uses representation selection and task
decomposition to improve performance ( Xu et al., 2026e ) . CDCR-SFT trains models
to construct causal graphs and reason over variable-level dependencies ( Li et al., 2025d ) . TAG-AD evaluates
contextual and structural anomalies in text-attributed graphs ( Xu et al., 2025a ) ; LLM-GOOD combines LLM filtering with graph neural networks
for data-efficient out-of-distribution detection ( Xu et al., 2025b ) .
ReMindRAG uses graph traversal and replay of earlier traversals to retrieve
relevant knowledge ( Hu et al., 2025 ) . These tasks differ in their outputs,
but all make the organization of information part of the reasoning problem.

Executable problems also support evaluation beyond a binary task outcome.
AlgoWorlds distinguishes feasible decisions from globally optimal ones using
exact solutions to combinatorial problems ( Xu et al., 2026d ) . QUITE
evaluates SQL rewrites for semantic equivalence and execution efficiency,
using database feedback during rewriting ( Song et al., 2025 ) . TerminalTraj
constructs agent trajectories in Dockerized environments and pairs them with
executable validation code ( Wu et al., 2026 ) .

CogWriter combines hierarchical planning with monitoring and revision for
constrained long-form generation ( Wan et al., 2025 ) . CoAct uses online
task allocation to parallelize LLM-agent execution ( Peng et al., 2026 ) .
Context-CoT synthesizes and filters reasoning traces grounded in supplied
context for fine-tuning ( Jin et al., 2026 ) , while AdaThinkV learns when
explicit reasoning improves video answers enough to justify its additional
response length ( Tian et al., 2026 ) .

Grid-Bench evaluates the complete spatial state produced by a supplied
transition sequence. History length counts events in this specification;

the output-level evaluation of spatial states.

blocks.en:
Controlled changes to an input provide another way to characterize model
behavior. Adaptive Distraction uses tree search to construct task-irrelevant
context while preserving the original question and answer ( Wang et al., 2025b ) . JevOut optimizes natural context additions to
redirect decisions under answer-preservation constraints ( Xu et al., 2026c ) .
Query-agnostic attacks on LLM retrieval show that document edits can also
change which evidence reaches a model ( Li et al., 2026a ) .
Cross-Lingual Pitfalls searches for bilingual questions that expose
performance discrepancies ( Xu et al., 2025c ) , and BICAUSE uses aligned
Chinese and English causal statements to examine sensitivity to language
and causal word order ( Wang et al., 2025a ) . These studies vary the
presentation surrounding a reasoning problem; Grid-Bench varies the supplied
events and spatial configurations that determine its reference outcome.

blocks.en:
Evaluation design also determines which aspects of a system become observable.
AutoBench-V generates images and visual questions to construct evaluations for
requested capabilities ( Bao et al., 2024 ) . AD-LLM separates anomaly
detection, data augmentation, and model selection into distinct tasks ( Yang et al., 2025 ) . Within logical reasoning, FineLogic distinguishes final
accuracy from stepwise soundness and representation-level evidence ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) . Agent evaluations make similar distinctions:
FORTIS separately checks skill selection and execution within permitted
actions ( Li et al., 2026d ) , while Counterfactual Trace Auditing compares
paired trajectories to identify behavioral changes that pass rates can miss ( Zhou et al., 2026b ) .

blocks.en:
Representational analyses and interventions address different questions from
output scoring. BiasLens measures associations among concepts in model
representations ( Gao et al., 2025 ) ; Treble Counterfactual VLMs uses causal
interventions to study modality shortcuts associated with hallucination ( Li et al., 2025c ) . Inside the Unfair Judge similarly studies scoring biases

generation with the LLM and acceptance with an independent semantic checker ( Zhou et al., 2026a ) . In Grid-Bench, reference execution supplies this
check: each returned cell is compared directly with its reference value.

STENCIL(a,r): simultaneously set every cell x with sum_i |x_i-a_i| <= r to (W(x) + sum W(y)) mod 4, where y ranges over the in-bounds cells at Manhattan distance 1 from x, whether or not they lie within distance r of a. Every update reads the same old world; cells farther than r from a remain unchanged.
blocks.zh: STENCIL. STENCIL(a,r):同时将每个单元格x与sum_i_x_i-a_i_i_<=r r设置为(W(x)+sum W(y))mod 4,其中y横跨曼哈顿距离1到x的内在细胞,无论它们是否位于a的距离r. 每一次更新都读取同一个旧世界;细胞比r更远,一个不变。

blocks.en: MIX. MIX(p,r): if W(p) = 0, nothing changes. Otherwise find every cell that can be reached from p by a path of at most r Manhattan-distance-1 steps whose cells all have nonzero old values (p itself counts as reached with 0 steps; a cell with old value 0 can never be entered or passed through). Then simultaneously set every reached cell x to 1 + ((W(x) + sum W(y)) mod 3), where y ranges over the in-bounds cells at Manhattan distance 1 from x, whether or not they were reached. Every update reads the old world; cells that were not reached remain unchanged.
blocks.zh: MIX. MIX(p,r):如果W(p)=0,则无变化. 否则就能找到每个从p到p的单元格,其途径最多为r 曼哈顿-距离-1步,其单元格都具有非零的旧值(p本身以0步计算;旧值0的单元格永远不能输入或传递). 然后同时将每个到达的单元格x到1+((W(x)+sum W(y))mod 3),其中y在曼哈顿距离x的1到x距离的输入细胞上范围,无论是否到达. 每一次更新都会读取旧世界;没有到达的单元格保持不变.

blocks.en: RELABEL. RELABEL(p,v): let u = W(p) (u may be 0). Find the maximal set of cells connected to p by Manhattan-distance-1 steps whose old values are all u, including p. Set every cell of that set to v.
blocks.zh: (原始内容存档于2019-03-03). RELABEL. RELABEL(p,v):让u=W(p)(u可能是0). 寻找由曼哈顿-距离-1步骤连接p的最大一组单元格,其旧值均为u,包括p. 设定该集的每个单元格为 v.

blocks.en: LAYER. LAYER(p,s): if W(p) = 0, nothing changes. Otherwise let u = W(p) and find the maximal Manhattan-connected set of cells with old value u, including p. If s = -1, set to 0 every cell of that set that has an in-bounds neighbor with old value 0. If s = +1, set to u every in-bounds cell with old value 0 that is a neighbor of a cell of that set. Positions outside the world are not neighbors; nothing else changes.
blocks.zh: LAYER. LAYER(p,s):如果W(p)=0,则无变化. 否则让 u = W(p) 找到包含 p 在内的具有旧值 u 的 最大曼哈顿连接的一组细胞. 如果 s = - 1, 设置为 0 , 那么该套集中每个有旧值的嵌入式相邻单元格 零点 如果 s = + 1, 设置为 u 每一个含有旧值 0 的单元格, 该单元格是该组合单元格的邻居 。 世界之外的位置不是邻居;其他情况也一样。

blocks.en: MOVE. MOVE(v,axis,direction,k): take every cell with value v, ordered by decreasing coordinate on axis if direction=1 and increasing if direction=-1, so that the cells nearest the leading edge are handled first. In that order, move each one along axis in the sign of direction, one cell at a time and at most k cells, stopping as soon as the next cell is outside the world or nonzero (including cells already moved into). Each move clears the old cell and writes v to the new cell; values never merge, and a block of adjacent v cells therefore moves as a unit.
blocks.zh: 走开。 MOVE(v,轴,指向,k):按每个带值的单元格v,如果方向=1,按轴上降低坐标排序,如果方向=1,则增加,这样,最接近前缘的单元格首先得到处理. 依此顺序,将每个细胞沿轴向的标志移动,一次一个细胞,最多一个k细胞,一旦下一个细胞处于世界之外或非零(包括已经移动的细胞)即停止. 每个动作清除旧单元格,并将 v 写到新单元格;数值永远不会合并,因此一个块相邻的 v 单元格会作为一个单元移动.

blocks.en: COMPRESS. COMPRESS(axis,direction): on every line parallel to axis, independently: list the nonzero values in order starting from the destination edge (coordinate 0 if direction=-1, the highest coordinate if direction=1). Walk that list from its start; whenever two consecutive values are equal, replace them by one value equal to their sum and continue after the pair, so a merged value cannot merge again in this event. Write the resulting list back starting at the destination edge and set every remaining cell of the line to 0.
